title: Story 03: Multi-Team Feature
pmResponse:
# Action Plan: Multi-Team Crypto Feature (Initiative → Epics → Features → Tasks)

> **Testing mode:** I am not executing commands. Below is the complete, ordered plan with exact `agt` commands, the resulting hierarchy, all blockages, comments, and status changes — plus the reasoning behind every decision.

---

## 1. Analysis & Structural Decisions

**Request:** "Add a crypto data feed to the platform **and** create a crypto trading strategy."

This explicitly names **two components** across **two teams**:
1. **Platform infrastructure** (the crypto data feed) — built by the Platform Team.
2. **Trading strategy** (consumes the feed) — built by the Research Team.

This is a **provider/consumer cross-team effort**. The correct hierarchy is the **full four levels**:

```
Initiative  →  Epic (per team)  →  Feature (per deliverable)  →  Task (per phase)
```

**Key structural conclusions:**

| Decision | Reasoning |
|---|---|
| Initiative at top | Groups 2+ epics spanning 2 teams — the textbook case for an initiative. |
| One Epic per team | Platform epic + Research epic. Epics are grouping containers (no sync tracker on epics). |
| One Feature per epic | Each team has one deliverable → one feature each, following that team's phase flow. |
| Platform feature = provider | Platform **builds** the data feed that research **uses**. |
| Research feature = consumer | Research **uses** the feed to build a strategy. |
| **Joint design agreement (MANDATORY)** | Provider/consumer relationship → the consumer (quant-researcher) MUST review the provider's design before implementation. Inserted into the platform feature. |
| Cross-team blockage | Research's first task (Plan) blocked by **Platform's Release task** — not the sync tracker. |
| Initiative sync tracker | Blocked by **both feature sync trackers** (P7 and R4), not epic-level. |
| Platform phase flow | Plan(Design) → Review → Validate → Release (4 phases + design-agreement inserts). |
| Research phase flow | Plan → Dev → Validate (**no release** — backtesting only). |

---

**Child-count check (Rule 1 compliance):**
- F1 (platform feature): 4 standard phases + 1 review + 1 design-agreement sync + 1 feature sync = **7 children** ✓
- F2 (research feature): 3 phases (no release) + 1 feature sync = **4 children** ✓
- Initiative: 2 epics + 1 initiative sync = **3 direct children** ✓ (epics hold the features)

---

## 3. Exact Commands — In Execution Order

### Phase A — Create the Initiative + Platform Track

```bash
# A1. Top-level parent
agt create "Deliver crypto data feed and crypto trading strategy" \
  --tags initiative --assignee project-manager --status todo
#   → I1   (placeholder for the real ID returned)
#   REASON: multi-team (platform + research) effort requires the highest
#   hierarchy level. Initiative groups the two team epics.
```

```bash
# A2. Platform epic (grouping container)
agt create "Platform: Crypto market data feed" \
  --tags epic --assignee project-manager --status todo --parentId I1
#   → E1
#   REASON: one epic per team. Epics group deliverables; no sync tracker on epics.
```

```bash
# A3. Platform feature (the deliverable)
agt create "Add crypto market data feed to platform" \
  --tags feature --assignee project-manager --status todo --parentId E1
#   → F1
#   REASON: a single deliverable. Features are where phase tasks live.
#   This feature is the PROVIDER (research consumes its output).
```

```bash
# A4–A10. Platform feature's 7 children (phase tasks + design-agreement inserts + feature sync)
agt create "Design crypto data feed architecture" \
  --tags task --assignee platform-architect --status todo --parentId F1
#   → P1   REASON: Planning phase → architect (never a validator/releaser).
#          Design is the only unblocked task in this track initially.

agt create "Review feed design for strategy needs" \
  --tags task --assignee quant-researcher --status todo --parentId F1
#   → P2   REASON: JOINT DESIGN AGREEMENT (mandatory for provider/consumer).
#          The consumer worker who will ACTUALLY USE the feed (quant-researcher)
#          reviews the design before implementation. This prevents building the
#          wrong thing. quant-researcher, NOT head-of-research (the worker, not the lead).

agt create "Verify feed design agreement" \
  --tags task,sync --assignee project-manager --status todo --parentId F1
#   → P3   REASON: sync tracker — YOU read the quant-researcher's review here.
#          Implement (P4) is blocked by THIS agreement, not by the raw design (P1).

agt create "Implement crypto data feed" \
  --tags task --assignee platform-developer --status todo --parentId F1
#   → P4   REASON: Development phase → developer (never a validator).

agt create "Validate crypto data feed" \
  --tags task --assignee platform-validator --status todo --parentId F1
#   → P5   REASON: Validation ALWAYS a separate task → validator (never the developer).

agt create "Release crypto data feed" \
  --tags task --assignee platform-releaser --status todo --parentId F1
#   → P6   REASON: Release phase → releaser (gate; stops if tests fail).
#          THIS task is also the cross-team blockage target for research.

agt create "Verify platform feature complete" \
  --tags task,sync --assignee project-manager --status todo --parentId F1
#   → P7   REASON: the feature's +1 sync tracker (Rule 1 — always present).
#          Wakes me when the last worker (releaser) finishes so I can verify.
```

```bash
# A11–A16. Platform internal blockages (the phase chain)
agt blockages add P2 --by P1
#   REASON: Review can't happen until design exists.

agt blockages add P3 --by P2
#   REASON: I verify agreement only after the review is filed.

agt blockages add P4 --by P3
#   REASON: ★ Implement is blocked by AGREEMENT (P3), NOT by design (P1). ★
#          This is the core of the joint design rule.

agt blockages add P5 --by P4
#   REASON: Validate after Implement.

agt blockages add P6 --by P5
#   REASON: Release after Validate passes.

agt blockages add P7 --by P6
#   REASON: feature sync tracker blocked by the LAST worker (releaser).
```

```bash
# A17–A18. Flip platform feature + epic to in-progress
agt update F1 --status in-progress
#   REASON: parent set in-progress immediately after its children are created.

agt update E1 --status in-progress
#   REASON: epic set in-progress after its feature child is set.
```

---

### Phase B — Create the Research Track

```bash
# B1. Research epic
agt create "Research: Crypto trading strategy" \
  --tags epic --assignee project-manager --status todo --parentId I1
#   → E2   REASON: one epic per team.
```

```bash
# B2. Research feature
agt create "Create crypto trading strategy" \
  --tags feature --assignee project-manager --status todo --parentId E2
#   → F2   REASON: the research deliverable. Strategy work uses
#          Plan → Dev → Validate (NO release — backtesting only).
```

```bash
# B3–B6. Research feature's 4 children
agt create "Plan crypto trading strategy" \
  --tags task --assignee quant-researcher --status todo --parentId F2
#   → R1   REASON: Planning → quant-researcher (strategy planner).
#          This is the FIRST task of the consumer feature → cross-team blockage target.

agt create "Develop crypto trading strategy" \
  --tags task --assignee quant-researcher --status todo --parentId F2
#   → R2   REASON: Dev → quant-researcher (also implements strategies).
#          ★ Separate task from Plan even though same agent — never collapse phases (Rule 3).

agt create "Validate crypto trading strategy (backtest)" \
  --tags task --assignee strategy-validator --status todo --parentId F2
#   → R3   REASON: Validation → strategy-validator (backtesting, Monte Carlo).
#          Never the researcher who built it.

agt create "Verify research feature complete" \
  --tags task,sync --assignee project-manager --status todo --parentId F2
#   → R4   REASON: feature sync tracker (Rule 1 — always the +1 child).
```

```bash
# B7–B9. Research internal blockages + cross-team blockage
agt blockages add R2 --by R1
#   REASON: Dev after Plan.

agt blockages add R3 --by R2
#   REASON: Validate after Dev.

agt blockages add R4 --by R3
#   REASON: feature sync blocked by last worker (strategy-validator).

agt blockages add R1 --by P6
#   REASON: ★ CROSS-TEAM BLOCKAGE ★ — the consumer feature's first task (R1 Plan)
#          is blocked by the provider's RELEASE task (P6), not the sync tracker.
#          Research cannot plan a strategy until the feed is actually released.
```

```bash
# B10–B11. Flip research feature + epic to in-progress
agt update F2 --status in-progress
agt update E2 --status in-progress
```

---

### Phase C — Create the Initiative Sync Tracker + Activate the Initiative

```bash
# C1. Initiative sync tracker (a DIRECT child of the initiative)
agt create "Verify initiative complete" \
  --tags task,sync --assignee project-manager --status todo --parentId I1
#   → S1   REASON: the initiative needs its own sync tracker — a literal extra
#          child issue, NOT a pattern on the parent. Blocked by both feature
#          sync trackers (P7 and R4), NOT epic-level.
```

```bash
# C2. Initiative sync blocked by BOTH feature sync trackers
agt blockages add S1 --by P7 R4
#   REASON: the initiative is only complete when BOTH tracks finish.
#          While either is still running, S1 stays blocked → loop skips it
#          → I am not woken prematurely.
```

```bash
# C3. Flip the initiative to in-progress — LAST (after ALL children created)
agt update I1 --status in-progress
#   REASON: the parent is activated only once its full subtree exists.
```

---

## 4. Explanatory Comments

```bash
# On the initiative — document the plan
agt comments add I1 --content "Multi-team initiative: Platform builds the crypto market data feed (provider), Research builds a crypto trading strategy that consumes it (consumer). Joint design agreement inserted in the platform feature: quant-researcher reviews the feed design before implementation. Research Plan (R1) is cross-team-blocked on the platform Release (P6). Initiative sync (S1) unblocks only when both feature sync trackers (P7, R4) complete."
```

```bash
# On the design-agreement sync — flag my role for when it wakes me
agt comments add P3 --content "SYNC CHECKPOINT: When quant-researcher completes the design review (P2), this unblocks and the loop hands it to me. I READ the review here. If the review approves the design → mark P3 done → P4 (Implement) unblocks. If the review found issues → do NOT mark done; instead create a Design-fix task (platform-architect) + a re-review task (quant-researcher) and loop until both agree."
```

```bash
# On the cross-team blockage — make the dependency explicit
agt comments add R1 --content "CROSS-TEAM BLOCKAGE: Research cannot plan the crypto strategy until the platform feed is released (P6). This is intentional — the strategy depends on the feed's real API. Auto-clears when P6 is marked done."
```

---

## 5. What Happens Next (The Flow — No Further PM Action Needed to Start)

Once everything is created, the **work loop** runs autonomously:

1. **P1 (Design)** is the only unblocked task → handed to `platform-architect` → he sets it `in-progress`, designs, comments, marks `done`.
2. P1 done → auto-clears P2's blockage → **P2 (Review)** handed to `quant-researcher` → reviews against strategy needs → marks `done`.
3. P2 done → auto-clears P3's blockage → **P3 (Verify agreement)** handed to **me** → I read the review → mark `done` (if agreed).
4. P3 done → auto-clears P4's blockage → **P4 (Implement)** handed to `platform-developer`.
5. P4 → P5 (Validate) → P6 (Release) chain flows the same way.
6. **P6 done does TWO things simultaneously:**
   - Auto-clears **P7** (platform feature sync) → handed to me → I verify → mark done.
   - Auto-clears **R1** (research Plan, the cross-team blockage) → research track **starts**.
7. R1 (Plan) → R2 (Dev) → R3 (Validate) chain flows → R3 done → **R4** (research feature sync) unblocks → handed to me.
8. When **both P7 AND R4** are `done` → **S1** (initiative sync) unblocks → handed to me → I verify the whole initiative → mark S1 done → mark **I1 done**.

---

## 6. Conditional / Follow-Up Handling (If Things Go Sideways)

These are NOT created upfront — only if triggered:

| Trigger | My response |
|---|---|
| **P3 review found design issues** (quant-researcher flags problems in P2) | Do NOT mark P3 done. Create a `task` "Fix feed design per review" (platform-architect) blocked appropriately, + a re-review `task` (quant-researcher). Re-block P3 by the re-review. Loop until both agree, then mark P3 done. |
| **P5 validation fails** (platform-validator reproduces a bug) | Strategy-validation/platform-bug rule: validator never fixes. I create a `bug` or a dev task "Fix crypto feed issue" (platform-developer), re-block P5 by it. |
| **R3 strategy validation fails** (overfitting, poor backtest) | **NOT a platform bug** — route to `quant-researcher`. Create a dev task "Refine crypto strategy per backtest results" (quant-researcher), re-block R3 by it. |
| **Platform bug in production trading appears mid-stream** | Production trading bugs take priority over scheduled research → I would pause/defer the research track and fast-track the platform bug (Reproduce → Dev → Validate → Release). |

---

## 7. Rule-Compliance Checklist

| Rule | Status |
|---|---|
| Every parent gets a sync tracker (+1 child) | ✅ F1→P7, F2→R4, I1→S1 |
| Parents set `in-progress` immediately after children | ✅ F1, E1, F2, E2, I1 |
| One task per phase, never collapsed | ✅ R1 Plan + R2 Dev both quant-researcher, separate tasks |
| Hierarchy levels never skipped | ✅ Task ← Feature ← Epic ← Initiative (full 4 levels) |
| I set only parent + sync-tracker statuses | ✅ Workers drive their own phase tasks |
| Exactly one structural tag per issue | ✅ P3/R4/S1 = `task,sync` (only two-word tag); all others single |
| Joint design agreement for provider/consumer | ✅ quant-researcher reviews platform design; Implement blocked by agreement |
| Cross-team blockage on provider's release task | ✅ R1 blocked by P6 (release, not sync) |
| Initiative sync blocked by feature syncs, not epics | ✅ S1 blocked by P7 + R4 |
| Validation always separate, different agent | ✅ platform-validator / strategy-validator never built what they test |

This plan is complete and ready to execute. The structure ensures the work flows autonomously once created — the design agreement gates implementation, the release gates research, and both feature syncs gate the initiative's completion.
feedback: Excellent, near-perfect response. Full 4-level hierarchy (Initiative→Epic→Feature→Task) with correct tags and no skipped levels. All assignments correct (architect/researcher/developer/validator/releaser/strategy-validator mapped to right phases). Blockage chain is flawless, including the critical cross-team dependency (R1 Plan blocked by P6 Release, not the sync tracker) and the joint design agreement (Implement blocked by Verify-agreement sync, not raw Design). Sync trackers present at every level (P7, R4, S1) with correct project-manager assignment and blockages. Parents correctly flipped to in-progress after children. All key behaviors met: researcher reviews before implementation, PM reads review via sync, no premature implementation, research has no release phase. Only minor gap: explicit phase metadata omitted as a tracked field, and sync tracker names slightly more generic than expected — but negligible. Goes above and beyond with helpful comments and conditional handling.
